A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the BAKE benchmark and reversal behavior in model editing, despite the changed title and research emphasis. Their complete text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original BAKE evaluations across four language models, BIRD results, probability analyses, and objective-weight sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports original editing evaluations in Tables 3 and 9, controlled ICL comparisons, output-error analyses, and concept-level experiments in Table 5.

M1.justification: BIRD's modifications to ROME, including objectives that strengthen new factual associations and weaken old ones bidirectionally, are removed (v2 Section 5). v3 Section 6.2 instead tests a procedure that applies existing editors and then supplies contextual examples during inference.

E1.justification: The BAKE-Q&J and BAKE-J factual coverage and reported dataset counts are retained. v3 Section 6.4 adds evaluation on 902 converted ConceptEdit-Inter/Intra examples, extending coverage from entity-relation facts to counterfactual modifications of natural-language concept definitions.

E2.justification: The BAKE comparisons remove KN and add RECT, AlphaEdit, GRACE, WISE, and IKE, while retaining FT, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME (v2 Table 3; v3 Tables 3 and 9). The tabulated unedited-model controls also disappear, although base-model comparisons remain in probability plots.

E3.justification: v3 rewrites the five principal metrics from pairwise probability comparisons to argmax correctness, although Section 3 retains a conflicting ES inequality. The stated template generator changes from gpt-3.5-turbo to gpt-4o. LLaMA-1 is removed, while LLaMA-3 8B, LLaMA-2 13B, and Qwen-3 8B are added. These are reported setting revisions, without establishing how experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2's BIRD objective-weight sensitivity study is removed. v3 adds comparisons with and without ICL for ROME, MEMIT, and WISE, an analysis of the first 1,000 IKE outputs, controlled forward-success case studies, and a test of reversal failure under conceptual edits (Sections 6.2–6.4). The existing probability analysis is retained with revised models and editors.

E5.justification: v2 Table 3 reports t-tests at p < 0.05 and marks significant BIRD improvements. v3 removes this testing statement and the significance markers, reporting point estimates without replacement uncertainty measures. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: Results change for retained combinations: LLaMA-2 7B ROME's BAKE-Q&J ES/RQS change from 99.70/0.26 to 99.39/0.32. BIRD and LLaMA-1 results disappear, while substantial new editor, model, ICL, and conceptual results appear; for example, v3 reports LLaMA-3 IKE RQS/RJS of 51.78/76.83. Changed metric definitions and template-generation settings prevent interpreting cross-version differences as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2's assumption connecting static-vector relationships to contextual representations, its relational derivation, and BIRD's mathematical objectives are removed. The detailed ROME formulation in Section 3.2 and Appendix A also disappears. Separately, v3 substantively revises the metric definitions to argmax correctness; renaming reversibility alone would not constitute this mathematical change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the contribution of a new mitigating method, BIRD, with a benchmark-centered investigation of reversal failure and possible mitigation through ICL. v3 qualifies failure as affecting most methods and emphasizes ICL's partial success and limitations. BAKE and the reverse-evaluation contribution remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations involving asymmetric conditional encoding, possible interference of parameter updates with ICL, and distributed conceptual representations. Limitations shift from BIRD's weak reverse-QA performance and untested parameter-preserving editors to ICL's lack of persistent memory, context constraints, and irrelevant outputs. Appendix F also develops the distinction between inverse-relation evaluation and multi-hop reasoning.

D1.justification: v3 removes BIRD's hyperparameter table and adds A800 80GB hardware, memory requirements, and runtime estimates in Appendix C. It provides additional editor code links and details of ICL inference and ConceptEdit conversion. The data/code availability statement changes from a future promise to stated availability, although the runtime discussion inconsistently still mentions BIRD.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning around parameter-preserving and ICL methods, newer reversal-curse studies, conceptual editing, and temporal or lifelong benchmarks. Added works include IKE, WISE, GRACE, ConceptEdit, TemporalWiki, and WikiBigEdit. The claimed relationship to prior research shifts from introducing BIRD to providing a single-edit evaluation and diagnostic analysis.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around evaluation and analysis. The BIRD section and ROME appendix are removed, a dedicated Analysis section is developed, and dataset details, supplementary results, and broader impact are reorganized. Reversibility is renamed reverse generalization throughout.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a predominantly single-column journal layout. Figure 1 is redrawn, probability plots are redesigned, and new ICL radar charts, response-distribution graphics, and case/concept tables appear. BIRD's diagram and sensitivity plot disappear. Benchmark results are split between the main text and Appendix D, while dataset statistics move to Appendix B.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses v2's explicit omission of parameter-preserving editors and provides a more informative account through ICL controls, failure cases, and concept-level evaluation. These strengthen the benchmark's usefulness. The improvement is limited by reporting inconsistencies: conflicting ES definitions in Section 3, MEMIT differences in Section 5.2 that do not match Table 3, and a runtime entry for the removed BIRD method.
